verdict.headline: US-Iran strikes resume after month-long pause; Brent crosses $90 on Strait mine threat
verdict.label: Brent $90.61; ES -0.1%; September hike odds 57%; 30Y at 5.21%, 9bps from trigger
verdict.rationale_short: CENTCOM struck rocket launchers on Iran's Larak Island on Sunday after the IRGC was observed readying sea mines for the Strait of Hormuz; Iran retaliated with ballistic missiles at US air bases in Jordan; a supertanker was mined and halted in the southern Strait. Brent jumped $2.39 to $90.61 while equity futures are contained at -0.1%, pricing a managed exchange rather than a Strait closure. If tanker transit suspends, $90 becomes a floor heading into the September 4 jobs print and September 16 FOMC — the same rate path the 30Y's 5.31% intraday near-breach last week had already flagged.

watchlist_mentions.note: ~$316.83 premarket (-0.72%). Tim Cook's final day; John Ternus officially becomes CEO September 1. The market has priced the transition since the April 20 announcement. The unresolved question is whether Ternus, a hardware engineer, articulates an AI platform vision at September's annual product event — that is the repricing risk, not today's session.

$219.07 premarket (+0.70% from Friday's $217.55 close). Partially recovering Friday's -4.57% session. Still below $220 structural support. Two closes above $225 on volume is the recovery criterion from the August 26-27 institutional buying zone at $215-220.

~$78,652 live (11:02 UTC). Weekend range $76,864-$79,409; $76,661 August 24 support has held through two retests. $80K two-close confirmation still open. Bessent buyback program starts September 9. Iran geopolitical risk adds a new variable — BTC can bid as a safe haven or sell with risk assets in sustained deleveraging.

trade_setups.thesis: Brent crossed $90 on the Larak Island exchange and a mined supertanker in the southern Strait — the first vessel halted by mines this cycle. The setup is a binary: if IRGC widens mine operations or tanker operators announce voluntary transit suspensions, $94-100 is the next structured zone; if the exchange is contained, Brent reverts toward $86-88. The $90 breach is the signal that the mine threat has been priced as real rather than rhetorical.
trade_setups.entry: $90 is the current breach level; $86-88 is the reversion zone if contained; $94 is the regime risk threshold
trade_setups.invalidation: A confirmed US-Iran pause via CENTCOM statement or Qatar mediation channel brings Brent below $87. Two consecutive tanker-transit-suspension announcements by a major operator confirms the escalation scenario.
trade_setups.horizon: 3-7 days; resolves with the September 4 jobs print or further military exchange

trade_setups.thesis: The 30Y touched 5.31% intraday last week before closing at 5.21% on August 28 — a near-breach without close confirmation, leaving 9bps of cushion. The oil channel is newly open: sustained Brent above $90 adds an estimated 20-30bps to headline CPI over 3-6 months and could enter Warsh communications before September 16. The Bessent buyback program starting September 9 provides structural demand estimated at 10-15bps of yield suppression.
trade_setups.entry: 5.21% is current; 5.30% is the regime close trigger; 5.00% is the dovish de-escalation level on a soft NFP
trade_setups.invalidation: NFP September 4 below 150K with AHE below 0.2% resets the 30Y toward 5.00-5.10%

trade_setups.thesis: At $219.07 premarket, NVDA is recovering Friday's -4.57% session but remains below $220 structural support. The August 26-27 institutional buying zone ($215-220) has not broken. Geopolitical risk sessions historically compress growth multiples; the floor holds or breaks on the first full session with Iran as a market backdrop.
trade_setups.entry: $215-220 is the support zone; $220 is the structural level; $225+ on two closes confirms the base held
trade_setups.invalidation: A daily close below $215 breaks the August 26-27 buying thesis and opens the $205-210 gap
trade_setups.horizon: This week; September 4 jobs report is the macro catalyst

bear_case: The scenario linking both stories: Brent sustaining above $94 concurrent with the 30Y closing above 5.30% would mark the first multi-indicator regime breach since the framework was constructed. This week's data stack amplifies the risk — a hot NFP (above 200K, AHE above 0.3%) locks in the September 16 hike while Canada's tariffs arrive September 8. If the Strait disruption pushes Brent toward $94-100, a third inflationary input enters Fed communications before September 16. If SPX closes below 7,650 in the first two sessions of this week, the current contained-exchange read is wrong.
